data.agent-vcs#Agent VCS:
A summary of forge/docs/agent-vcs.md, the authoritative text (design approved 2026-11-25). Where the two differ, the source document wins.
Design stage, not implemented. Nothing on this page runs yet. It extends the design and inherits all of its invariants.
data.constraints#Constraints: git stays the storage and interchange format: git clone, git fetch and mirroring to GitHub keep working unchanged. The design’s invariants hold: no secret in argv, environment or URL; every untrusted parser fuzzed; every input bounded. A branch moves only to the exact commit CI judged green. No “merge, then let an agent fix it”. Every write is idempotent under retry with the same request id.
data.forge-agentd#Local daemon: forge-agentd: One per user per machine, and the only process that talks to the server. It serves local sessions over a Unix socket (peer uid checked), keeps a content-addressed object cache (an object is admitted only after its id is recomputed from its content), can Materialize a sparse checkout into a directory the caller owns, and fans one upstream event stream out to local subscribers, so N waiters cost one stream, not N pollers. Its first backend is GitHub (milestone A0), which does not wait for the forge.
data.inspiration#Inspiration:
This design is inspired by Anthropic’s account of its internal agent-oriented source control. Scion is Anthropic’s internal system and has not been released; go-vcs has no affiliation with Anthropic and is not endorsed by it. The agent layer is an independent design on top of git.
“Redesigning source control at Anthropic”, Anthropic Engineering, 2026-10-13 (updated 2026-10-15): https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/redesigning-source-control. It also mentions Antique, Anthropic’s code review tool, which is not described in a post of its own. Taken from it: server-side reads and writes without a clone, stable change identity, server-side merge gated on CI for the exact commit, path leases, one local daemon, atomic multi-repository changes. Not taken: merge-then-fix, Spanner, FUSE checkouts.
data.milestones#Milestones: A0: forge-agentd with a GitHub backend: local protocol, verified object cache, Materialize, one poller per machine, WaitVerdict answered from the stream. Operations that need the forge answer UNSUPPORTED_BY_BACKEND, never a weaker imitation. Comes first. A1 (after forge milestone 4): reads without a clone, CreateChange, revision refs, server-signed commits, compare-and-swap ref updates, idempotent writes, agent-session identities. A2 (after milestone 5): verdicts, merge gated on them and on signed human approval, event stream. A3: leases with fencing epochs, path permissions. A4: the forge backend of forge-agentd. A5: atomic multi-repository change sets.
data.the-layer#The layer: Change ids. A stable id for a change across amends and rebases, with immutable revision refs. CI verdicts bound to the exact commit. A verdict names the full object id it judged; a merge names the revision it intends to merge. Server-side merge. merge-tree computes the result without a checkout, and the ref moves by compare-and-swap, so concurrent merges need no manual “update branch”. Path leases. Leases on paths with fencing epochs, replacing whole-repository, silently lapsing leases. Reads and writes without a clone. Trees, blobs, diffs and CreateChange at any revision, over gRPC. Atomic multi-repository change sets. Joint CI and a two-phase merge, at most 64 repositories. Human approval. Merges to protected refs need a FIDO2-signed approval. Server-signed commits.
data.why#Why: The forge’s first users are not only people: on one build machine about 25 coding-agent sessions run at once against many repositories, through plain git and the GitHub API. The design answers frictions measured there: worktrees and clones lost or duplicated, a full commit id rebuilt from a 7-character prefix, a CI verdict left on the commit before an amend, concurrent merges into one branch, whole-repository leases that lapse silently, many CI pollers sharing one rate-limit budget, and dependent changes spread over many repositories.

data.actions#Actions: The forge serves the gitea-runner protocol so that the existing runner runs our jobs unchanged. Registration tokens are single-use, short-lived and bound to one runner name; a job’s token is scoped to its repository and job and revoked when the job ends; secrets are never sent to runs triggered from forks. Runners are created by GARM, first through its gitea forge type, later through a govcs type to be contributed to GARM.
data.administration#Administration: Everything administrative goes through one gRPC API, and the web UI has no admin page the API lacks. Authentication is a FIDO2 credential on a hardware key with user verification. Enrolment verifies the attestation against FIDO MDS3 and accepts only allowlisted AAGUIDs, with no opt-out. Each mutating call carries a fresh assertion over a challenge that combines a server nonce, the hash of the exact request message and a TLS exporter value of the connection, so an assertion is valid for one request on one connection.
data.design#Design: A summary of forge/docs/design.md, which is the authoritative text (draft of 2026-11-25) and cites the source it read for every claim. Where the two differ, the design document wins.
data.git-transport#Git transport: SSH and smart HTTP, protocol v2 only for fetch. Push policy is decided in-process by parsing the receive-pack command list and pack with gitproto before any ref moves: there are no server-side hooks and no internal callback token.
data.identity#Identity: Web sign-in goes only through the go-authn bridge (OIDC), with a client restricted to the bridge’s local accounts. The forge implements no passwords. A sign-in whose issuer and subject are not bound to an existing account is refused: it never creates an account and never links to a signed-in session. SSH push and pull use per-user SSH keys, preferably FIDO-backed sk- keys.
data.milestones#Milestones: gitproto: pkt-line, protocol v2 capability advertisement, ls-refs and fetch, with fuzzers and a benchmark against git upload-pack. forge: storage layout, accounts, admin gRPC API with FIDO2 assertions and its CLI; SSH and HTTP clone. Implemented: fetch is protocol v2 only and read only (git-upload-pack); push is refused with a message naming milestone 4. Repositories live at //.git; a reader must be the owner, or the repository must hold a git-daemon-export-ok file (anonymous HTTP read is public repositories only). A missing and a forbidden repository give the same answer. SSH uses the per-user keys of the admin API and runs git-upload-pack only (no shell, pty, forwarding or agent); HTTP is TLS 1.3, anonymous, and refuses protocol v0/v1, the dumb protocol and receive-pack with a message that says why. Each transport bounds request size, pkt-line count, time per request, and concurrent sessions per account (per address over HTTP) and in total. forge: OIDC sign-in through the bridge, read-only web UI. gitproto and forge: receive-pack with in-process push policy. A1 (agent-oriented layer, see Agent VCS): read and write without a clone, stable change ids and immutable revision refs, server-signed commits, compare-and-swap ref updates, idempotent writes, agent-session identities. actions: workflow planning, runner protocol server, GARM gitea type. A2: CI verdicts bound to the exact commit, server-side merge gated on them and on a FIDO2-signed human approval for protected refs, event stream. A3: path-scoped leases, path permissions. A4: the forge backend of forge-agentd. A5: atomic multi-repository change sets (at most 64 repositories). Pull requests and reviews in the web UI. GARM govcs forge type; artifacts. A0, the local daemon forge-agentd with a GitHub backend, does not depend on the milestones above and comes first (see Agent VCS).
data.status#Status: Milestone 2 (the admin gRPC API and its CLI; clone and fetch over SSH and smart HTTP) is implemented. The rest is not.
data.three-repositories#Three repositories: Repository Holds gitproto Git wire protocol v2 (upload-pack, receive-pack), pkt-line, pack files and indexes. A library with no forge knowledge, fuzzed and benchmarked against git. actions Workflow parsing and planning (matrix, needs, expressions) and the server side of the gitea-runner protocol. Reusable without the forge. forge The server: storage, accounts, permissions, SSH and smart HTTP transports, web UI, admin gRPC API and its CLI, webhooks, the GARM-facing API.

data.forge-agentd#forge-agentd: forge-agentd is the first implemented slice of Agent VCS (milestone A0): a local daemon with a GitHub backend, and forge-agent, the small client agents call. Source and releases: go-vcs/agentd.
data.guarantees#What it gives an agent: No token in the agent. The daemon reads one token from a file (mode 0600, never from argv, environment or URL); agents talk to it over a unix socket (directory 0700, socket 0600, peers of another uid dropped). A verdict bound to one exact commit. Object ids are full (40 or 64 lowercase hex); an abbreviation is refused, never expanded. Only the newest run per (workflow, event) counts, a run with zero jobs is never green, a null conclusion or an unknown job count is pending, and an observation about another commit is refused. One poller per commit. Any number of waiters on the same commit cost one upstream poll loop, so they share one rate-limit budget. A gated merge. merge succeeds only if the commit named is still the pull request’s head and its verdict is green; otherwise REF_MOVED (naming the current commit), VERDICT_RED or VERDICT_PENDING. GitHub’s own sha precondition closes the remaining race. Idempotent writes. A 32-hex request id replays the first answer; the same id with another body is REQUEST_ID_REUSED. Structured errors. {"error":{"reason":"...","retryable":...}}, and a per-session identity from hello.
data.status#Status: Done: verdicts, waits, gated merge, idempotency, sessions, the socket, structured errors, fuzzed parsers. Not done: the verified object cache, Materialize, a push event stream (the hub polls), a keychain credential option. Leases, changes and change sets answer UNSUPPORTED_BY_BACKEND until the forge backend exists.
data.use#Use: forge-agentd --token-file ~/.github-token forge-agent --label build-7 verdict go-vcs/forge <40-hex-commit> forge-agent --label build-7 wait go-vcs/forge <40-hex-commit> --timeout 20m forge-agent --label build-7 merge go-vcs/forge 6 <40-hex-commit> Exit codes: 0 green or done, 1 error, 3 red or refused by the gate, 4 pending or timed out. merge prints its request id on stderr so a retry can reuse it with --request-id.
